summary: Mathews County, VA steel lookout tower announced in April 1938 and described in a 1942 survey note as 100 ft with glass cab; FFLA lists it standing; no staffing, access or current condition found.

facts.design: Four-legged steel tower about 100 ft high with a glass-enclosed cab (1942 survey description)
facts.status_note: Listed as standing by FFLA; the 2002 survey note concerns the survey mark, not the tower
facts.agency: Virginia Department of Forestry (Forest Lookouts header); 1938 announcement says the state forest service, a division of the Virginia conservation commission, would erect it

access.note: No public access information in the sources read; ask the Virginia Department of Forestry before visiting

events.note: Construction announced in April 1938 for that spring; completion date not given in the sources
Coast and Geodetic Survey description of the tower: four-legged steel, about 100 ft, glass cab, owned and operated by the state forest service
Recovery note on survey mark GV4242 by US Power Squadron: recovered in good condition (refers to the survey mark)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Not resolved. The 1938 announcement gives a point on Highway 14 about 1.5 miles east of Foster; the 1942 description gives about 4.1 miles NE of the town of Mathews. The record's coordinates come from the FFLA list and were not checked against either description.

notes_for_editor: Built date is only the spring-1938 announcement; no completion report found. Location descriptions conflict (see resolved_conflicts) and the record coordinates were not tested against them. The 2002 'good condition' note is about the survey mark, not the tower; do not read it as a condition assessment. No staffing history or access information found. The 1942 description is from a Coast and Geodetic Survey station description quoted in the NGS datasheet. Do not confuse with the Matthews State Forest lookout (Grayson County, ex-Morris Knob tower), which appeared in a search snippet only and was not read. Two web searches used.
